# 1.2.48 - the second audit of 1.2.42, and what the live table found

1.2.43 to 1.2.47 came out of one audit of 1.2.42. A second, separate review of
the same version ran alongside it, in five stages, and never reached a release
because the two lines had not been joined. This is them joined: 150 changes of
the second review folded into everything 1.2.47 shipped, the handful of places
where the two had built the same thing settled in favour of the one your world
already stores data in, and then the defects the live table found this week.

Nothing here asks a world to be migrated. Where both lines built the same
feature - the sentence a trace reveals when it is analysed is the visible one -
1.2.47's field names are kept, because a world running 1.2.47 already holds
them.

## The Class Trial has an economy

A trial used to be the one scene where nothing cost anything. Now:

- **A Class Trial opens with the time of day's actions**, and keeps a Burst or a
  Sprint somebody bought with Hope. It does this on every road into a trial -
  the Start button, a debate opened on its own, the campaign editor - and only
  once: a trial's second debate refills nothing.
- **Only Analyze and an Objection are open in a trial**, plus the Hope Calls.
- **An Objection and an Analyze pay the same chain: an action, then Hope, then a
  Sanity mark.** The tile shows the price it is about to charge before you press
  it, and a student with nothing left can still Present.
- **Tamper costs one thing, not two:** an action, or a Sanity mark. A critical
  gives back the step that paid.

## New for the GM

- **A Level Up can be handed to the player.** The GM decides what was earned,
  standard or reinforced, and then who picks. The player's Level Up button
  lights gold, they choose, and the GM's client checks the choice against the
  offer and writes it. The offer lives where no player can forge it and nobody
  else can read it - after a wrong verdict, who holds a Reinforced Level Up is
  the name of the killer.
- **A reshaped trace waits for your ruling.** A Tamper that rewrites a trace
  sends you a card with the player's name and sentence for it; nothing is
  written until you approve. Declining is a ruling, not a refund. A Reroll
  voids the older card, and a story declined on a critical erase still erases.
- **New trace**, on the case panel: put a trace of any kind the map can hold,
  in any room, with its two flags - part of the murder, reinforced - asked
  rather than assumed.
- **A project token opens a card**, like a trace: name, progress, room for the
  people who know it; for the GM also who may see it, who already does, and
  the trigger of a murder.
- **The clock names the track you are hearing** - read from what this browser
  is actually playing, so a cue the GM auditions never reaches a player's clock.
- **Your own token wears the hour** - a ring in the time of day's colour, on your
  screen only.
- **A season reset keeps whatever you untick**, in 27 groups, remembered for the
  next reset.
- **A project's viewers are a list of players**, ticked where you already are.

## The look

- **Monokuma Legacy follows the Interface scale**, as Stained Glass always has.
  The smallest sizes are floored so the slider cannot shrink them past reading,
  and a client that never touches the slider sees nothing change.
- **High contrast is a switch**, and reduced motion is one in both themes.
- **An ultrawide screen stops stretching the module.**
- **A window under the glass arrives frosted.** It used to arrive sharp and snap
  to frosted on its last frame: a fading window cannot blur what is behind it.
  Windows also close without waiting a second any more.

## Fixed, from the live table

- **A rerolled Analyze that lost erased the GM's own sentence** from the trace,
  and from there from every copy in every pack. It takes back only what it
  published now, and the Faint badge with it.
- **Double-clicking a trace opened Daggerheart's adversary sheet** instead of the
  trace's card: 1.2.47's card threw on a missing line. And every NPC sheet - a
  trace's, a project's - printed its name one letter per line, squeezed into the
  character sheet's rail. Both fixed.
- **Under Monokuma Legacy the Event panel stood above Despair Pools.**
- **Clicking the word "Day" in Edit campaign moved the campaign back a day.** The
  number steppers put their minus button first inside each field's label, and a
  label presses the first thing it can - since 06.09, on every labelled number
  field. The label points at the field now.
- **An assistant GM's Despair was still written locally**, the race 1.2.47 set
  out to close still open. It reaches the primary GM now.
- **A deferred assembly run while the GM looked at another map moved nobody.**
- **The overflow's Silence shut a Monokuma's Despair Calls.** It shuts the
  students' Hope Calls, as the handbook says, and nothing else.
- **"Nothing was there" told the player their action was back** while charging
  their Sanity. It says what happened now.
- **Every control in the GM's windows has a name** a screen reader can say -
  about 180 of them, table rows that only their column headers had named.

## The economy, made to add up

The review's second stage was one long look at what gets charged and what comes
back, and most of it is invisible when it works:

- One action buys one roll, however many roll windows are open; a closed window
  refunds only an action whose roll never counted.
- A refund gives back exactly the step its spend was paid with.
- A Despair Call that would change nothing is refused before it is paid, and
  refusals come before the picker rather than after the confirmation.
- A Hope Call the GM approves is charged against the Hope held at the yes.
- Every Reroll is scored by the rules the action used, settles Hope and Sanity
  like any roll, and keeps its Hope and Fear colours in Dice So Nice.
- Under the Despair darkening, refunds still arrive and Hope that cannot land is
  not sold.
- Seals, chains and Silence end when the Eclipse opens.
- **Pain costs four Despair.**

## Smaller

- A trial has one verdict, locked before anything is asked.
- A body is discovered once, from every route, and only a body counts.
- An assembly leaves the dead where they fell.
- Isometric Perspective and LiveKit are recommended, not required.
- Everything new is in Polish as well.

268 regression tests pass on a live world, including scenarios that drive two
clients at once for the handed-over Level Up and the assistant GM's Despair.
